title: Search a 2D Matrix
prompt: You are given an `m x n` integer matrix `matrix` with the following properties: each row is sorted in non-decreasing order, and the first integer of each row is greater than the last integer of the previous row. Given an integer `target`, return `true` if `target` is in `matrix`, or `false` otherwise. Your solution must run in `O(log(m * n))` time.
hints: Scanning every row and column works in O(m*n), but the row-major ordering means the whole matrix behaves like one long sorted array.
Treat the matrix as a single sorted array of length m*n and binary search over indices 0..m*n-1.
Convert a flat index back to (row, col) using integer division and modulo by the row width.

solution.approach: Because each row is sorted and every row starts after the previous row ends, the entire matrix is equivalent to one sorted array of length m*n when read in row-major order. Binary search over flat indices 0 to m*n - 1, converting each mid index to (row, col) via divmod by the column count, and compare matrix[row][col] to target just like a standard sorted-array binary search. This achieves O(log(m*n)) time without ever materializing the flattened array.
